hints.content: The graph of function $h$ is the graph of function $g$ shifted left $5$ units and up $1$ unit.

To shift the graph of $y=g(x)$ left $5$ units, we can replace $x$ with $x+5$ in the equation. 


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two congruent parabolas labeled g of x and g of x plus five in parentheses on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph labeled g of x has a vertex at (zero, seven) and has an interval of increase from negative six to zero and an interval of decrease from zero to six. The graph labeled g of x plus five in parentheses has a vertex at (negative five, seven) and has an interval of increase from negative ten to negative five and an interval of decrease from negative five to one.

hints.content:
To shift the graph of $y=g(x+5)$ up $1$ unit, we replace $g(x+5)$ with $g(x+5)+1$ in the equation.

[[☃ image 1]]

Notice that this is the graph of function $h$, and so $h(x)=g(x+5)+1$.

options.alt: Three congruent parabolas labeled g of x, g of x plus five in parentheses, and g of x plus five in parentheses plus one on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one.  The graph labeled g of x has a vertex at (zero, seven) and has an interval of increase from negative six to zero and an interval of decrease from zero to six. The graph labeled g of x plus five in parentheses has a vertex at (negative five, seven) and has an interval of increase from negative ten to negative five and an interval of decrease from negative five to one. The graph labeled g of x plus five in parentheses plus one has a vertex at (negative five, eight) and has an interval of increase from negative ten to negative five and an interval of decrease from negative five to one.
